theater: 福岡縣秋月至豐津一帶

battle.name: 秋月之亂
battle.theater: 福岡縣秋月至豐津一帶
battle.brief: 一八七六年十月二十七日，舊秋月藩士宮崎車之助、今村百八郎等約四百人舉兵，響應三日前熊本的神風連之亂，在明元寺殺害縣警官穗波半太郎；二十九日北進豐津，遭小倉駐屯的熊本鎮台步兵第十四連隊擊潰，戰死十七人，隊伍旋即瓦解。同週的熊本，線膛砲所在的砲兵營正是被叛軍一度奪取的目標。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰一方是舊秋月藩士組成的秋月黨：約四百人，以今村百八郎為隊長，骨幹為宮崎車之助、磯淳、戶原安浦、磯平八、戶波半九郎、宮崎哲之助、土岐清、益田靜方等舊藩家臣，分隊行動，裝備是舊藩刀與少量小銃，沒有騎兵，也沒有任何火砲。另一方是明治政府的常備軍與治安機關：主戰兵力是熊本鎮台步兵第十四連隊，駐紮小倉，連隊長心得乃木希典；福岡縣一帶另有縣警察與縣廳的治安兵力，討伐本部設在秋月小學。鎮台是明治初年最大的常備編制單位，全國分六管鎮台警衛，熊本鎮台管轄筑前、筑後、肥前、肥後一帶，鎮台下設步兵與砲兵大隊。豐津一方的舊豐津藩士杉生十郎等原已與秋月黨約定同時舉兵，事到臨頭改為不動並被拘禁，談判由此拖延了叛軍北進的時間。
countriesEn: One belligerent was the Akizuki party, a band formed from the samurai of the former Akizuki domain: about four hundred men, with Imanaga Hyakuhachiro as commander and a core of former retainers such as Miyazaki Kuranosuke, Iso Jun, Tohara Yasuura, Iso Heihachi, Tonami Hankuro, Miyazaki Tetsunosuke, Toki Kiyoshi and Masuda Shizukata. They moved in separate bands, armed with old domain swords and a few handguns, with no cavalry and not a single piece of artillery. The other side was the standing army and the security organs of the Meiji government. The main fighting force was the 14th Infantry Regiment of the Kumamoto Garrison, stationed at Kokura and led by Nogi Maresuke as regimental commander designate; in Fukuoka Prefecture the prefectural police and the prefectural administration supplied security detachments, and a suppression headquarters was set up in the primary school at Akizuki. The garrison was the largest permanent formation of the early Meiji army, the country being divided into six garrison districts; Kumamoto Garrison covered Chikuzen, Chikugo, Hizen and Higo, and each garrison held infantry and artillery battalions. In Toyotsu the former Toyotsu domain samurai, Sugo Juro among them, had originally pledged to rise at the same moment; at the last moment they decided against it and were locked up instead, and the ensuing negotiations held up the rebels' advance to the north.
people: 叛軍一方，今村百八郎以隊長身份主持舉兵，事後仍帶二十六人返回秋月攻擊討伐本部，最終被捕並在十二月初三日斬首；宮崎車之助是舊秋月藩的核心人物，與磯淳、土岐清等七名士族在江川村栗河內自刃；益田靜方在舉兵前一日前往佐賀呼應舊佐賀藩士，途中即被捕，事後同樣被處斬；戶波半九郎的辭世句今日收藏於朝倉市秋月博物館。官軍一方，乃木希典在明治八年十二月出任熊本鎮台步兵第十四連隊長心得，常駐小倉；此職之所以出缺，正因前任山田頴太郎被疑同情反亂士族而被免職。乃木的內弟玉木正誼曾屢次勸他響應前原一誠，他不從，反把此事向陸軍卿山縣有朋報告。福原和勝事後以書信批評他在萩之亂中未動第十四連隊。縣警官穗波半太郎在明元寺遇害，成為福岡縣警首位殉職者。同週在熊本，鎮台司令官種田政明與參謀長高島茂德戰死，敬神黨領袖太田黑伴雄重傷之後自刃。
peopleEn: On the rebel side, Imanaga Hyakuhachiro directed the rising as commander and afterwards still led twenty-six men back into Akizuki to assault the suppression headquarters; he was finally arrested and beheaded on 3 December. Miyazaki Kuranosuke was a core figure of the old Akizuki domain and cut his own throat in the valley at Kakkawa-uchi in Egawa village together with six other samurai including Iso Jun and Toki Kiyoshi. Masuda Shizukata had set out for Saga on the day before the rising to call on the former Saga domain samurai, was arrested on the way, and was likewise sentenced to death; the death poem of Tonami Hankuro is today kept in the Akizuki Museum of Asakura City. On the government side, Nogi Maresuke took up the post of commander designate of the 14th Infantry Regiment of the Kumamoto Garrison in December 1875 and was stationed at Kokura; the vacancy arose precisely because his predecessor, Yamada Eitaro, had been relieved of command on suspicion of sympathy with rebellious samurai. Nogi's brother-in-law, Tamaki Masayoshi, urged him more than once to throw in his lot with Maehara Kazunori; Nogi refused and instead reported the matter to Army Minister Yamagata Aritomo. Later Fukahara Kazukatsu criticised Nogi in a letter for not moving the 14th Regiment during the Hagi rising. Prefectural police officer Hokami Hantarō was killed at Myogenji and became the first Fukuoka prefectural police officer to die on duty. In Kumamoto in the same week, the garrison commander Tane Seihei and the chief of staff Takashima Shigetoku were killed in action, and the Shinpuuren leader Otaguro Tomoo cut his own throat after being mortally wounded.
kits: 線膛砲的前裝線膛野戰砲，是一八五○年代普魯士砲兵的制式化裝備，六磅級與十二磅級的線膛砲相繼列裝，射程因此遠於滑膛砲；到一八八○年前後，日本陸軍才系統性換裝後裝的七五糎野戰砲。一八七六年秋月之亂發生時，鎮台砲兵仍以前裝線膛野戰砲與山砲為主力，熊本鎮台轄下有砲兵第六大隊。同月十月二十四日深夜，熊本的敬神黨襲擊鎮台，奪取了砲兵營及其所藏的火砲與彈藥，砲兵營因此成為那一夜最被爭奪的目標。步兵方面，陸軍主力是小銃與舊式刀劍；西南戰爭中官軍還使用四斤山砲這類小口徑前裝火砲。秋月黨沒有制式火砲，武器是舊藩刀與少量手裝小銃，彈藥自備而數量有限，運輸依靠馬匹與人力，沿筑後平原的道路北進，秋月到豐津的一段須在丘陵與水田之間的窄路上行軍。
kitsEn: The rifled muzzle-loading field gun was the standardised weapon of Prussian artillery in the 1850s, with rifled six-pounder and twelve-pounder pieces entering service in turn and out-ranging the old smoothbores; only around 1880 did the Japanese army systematically replace them with breech-loading 75 mm field guns. When the Akizuki rising took place in 1876, garrison artillery was still armed chiefly with rifled muzzle-loading field guns and mountain guns, and the Kumamoto Garrison had an artillery battalion of its own. On the night of 24 October in the same month the Shinpuuren in Kumamoto struck the garrison, seized the artillery barracks and the guns and ammunition stored in it, and the barracks consequently became the most contested prize of that night. On the infantry side the army's main weapons were small arms and old swords; in the Seinan War the government side also used small-calibre muzzle-loading pieces such as the four-pounder mountain gun. The Akizuki party had no service artillery at all, only old domain swords and a few handguns with ammunition of its own and in short supply, and it moved north on the roads across the Chikugo plain on horses and on foot, the march from Akizuki to Toyotsu running along narrow lanes between hills and paddy fields.
tactics: 秋月黨的戰術是夜襲式的突然舉兵：十月二十七日入夜，黨人先在明元寺以勸說為名接近並殺害縣警官穗波半太郎，再逐村號召舊藩士，同時派人聯絡豐津與佐賀，計劃由秋月向縣廳與熊本方向進逼，與神風連、萩之亂互相呼應。政府軍的戰術建立在情報與攔截之上：乃木靠密偵與偵察掌握叛軍北進的動向，第十四連隊由小倉出發，在豐津以行軍縱隊攔截；接戰後以步槍射擊與刺刀衝鋒迫近，叛軍戰死十七人、政府軍戰死二人，隨即退向江川村栗河內。砲兵在這種近距離的丘陵與村落戰中難以展開，決定勝負的仍是步槍射程與白刃。對照同月萩的亂，官軍除広島鎮台的步兵外，還有軍艦孟春自海上向叛軍攻擊，可見砲兵與海軍火力對付士族暴動的決定性。地形上，秋月位於筑後盆地北緣，豐津在它北面約三十公里，中間隔著江川丘陵與大片水田。
tacticsEn: The tactic of the Akizuki party was a sudden night rising: on the evening of 27 October the conspirators first approached the prefectural police officer Hokami Hantaro at Myogenji on the pretext of persuasion and killed him, then called up former domain men village by village, sent messengers to Toyotsu and Saga, and planned to press from Akizuki towards the prefectural offices and Kumamoto so as to act in concert with the Shinpuuren rising and the Hagi rising. The government's method rested on intelligence and interception: Nogi learned of the rebels' northward move through agents and reconnaissance, marched the 14th Regiment out of Kokura, and caught them on the march at Toyotsu. After contact was made the government infantry closed with rifle fire and the bayonet, and the rebels, with seventeen dead against two government dead, fell back to Kakkawa-uchi in Egawa village. Artillery could hardly be deployed in a close fight among hills and villages, and the outcome was settled by rifle range and cold steel. By contrast, in the Hagi rising of the same month the government fielded infantry of the Hiroshima Garrison together with the warship Moshun, which engaged the rebels from the sea, showing how decisive artillery and naval gunfire could be against a samurai rising. Topographically, Akizuki lies on the northern rim of the Chikugo basin, about thirty kilometres south of Toyotsu, with the hills of Egawa and wide paddy fields in between.
data: 秋月黨的規模，史料記載為約四百人，首領名單可辨者十一人；政府軍方面，投入豐津方向的兵力以熊本鎮台步兵第十四連隊為主，具體到該役的分隊人數未見記載，能確定的戰果數字是秋月黨戰死十七人、政府軍戰死二人。時間線是：十月二十七日舉兵，二十九日抵豐津交戰，三十日退入江川村栗河內，三十一日隊伍解散；今村百八郎十一月二十四日在逃亡途中被捕，十二月初三日福岡臨時裁判所宣判，今村與益田靜方即日斬首，約一百五十名同黨受懲役、除族等處分。同期數字可作對照：神風連之亂中敬神黨死者及自刃者一百二十四人，約五十人被捕，官軍死者約六十人、負傷者約二百人；萩之亂前原一誠等號稱二百人，亦有五百零六人乃至二千餘人的異說。制度面的數字是：明治九年八月的秩祿處分將年俸百石以下削至五分之一，百石以上五百石以下削至三分之一，五百石以上削至四分之一；同年三月二十八日頒布廢刀令。
dataEn: The size of the Akizuki party is recorded as about four hundred men, with eleven leaders whose names can be read; on the government side the force sent towards Toyotsu was centred on the 14th Infantry Regiment of the Kumamoto Garrison, and no record survives of the number of sub-units committed, the only firm casualty figures being seventeen of the Akizuki party dead against two of the government troops. The chronology runs: rising on 27 October, arrival at Toyotsu and fighting on the 29th, retreat into Kakkawa-uchi in Egawa village on the 30th, dissolution of the band on the 31st; Imanaga Hyakuhachiro was arrested while fleeing on 24 November, and on 3 December the Fukuoka Temporary Court pronounced sentence, Imanaga and Masuda Shizukata being beheaded on the spot and about one hundred and fifty of their fellows sentenced to penal servitude, removal from clan and the like. Figures from the same weeks give a scale of comparison: in the Shinpuuren rising one hundred and twenty-four of the Shinpuuren died or killed themselves, about fifty were taken, and the government lost about sixty dead and about two hundred wounded; in the Hagi rising Maehara Kazunori and his colleagues claimed two hundred men, though figures of five hundred and six or of more than two thousand are also given. The institutional figures are these: the stipend settlement of August 1876 cut annual pensions below one hundred koku to one fifth, those from one hundred to five hundred koku to one third, and those above five hundred koku to one quarter; the sword ban was promulgated on 28 March of the same year.
cause: 起事的根子在明治政府對舊藩士的兩刀：一八七一年廢藩置縣解散了藩兵，士族失去藩的俸祿與編制；明治九年三月二十八日的廢刀令限制佩刀，八月的秩祿處分又大幅削減俸祿，使秋月、豐津、佐賀一帶的中下級藩士在數月之間由衣食無憂變為入不敷出。背景還有自由民權運動與徵韓論之後的政治氣氛：西鄉隆盛辭職返鄉，薩摩的私學校設有銃隊學校與砲隊學校，同輩之間以學校、藩校與同鄉的關係維繫著反骨的計畫，而地方官廳以警察取代舊藩的治安功能，衝突遲早會發生。直接導火線是十月二十四日深夜熊本的神風連之亂——敬神黨襲擊鎮台司令官與縣令的住宅，佔領砲兵營，翌日被鎮壓。消息三日內傳到筑後，秋月黨原本就與豐津藩士有同時舉兵的約定，於是十月二十七日依約在夜間集合動手。
causeEn: The roots of the rising lay in the two cuts the Meiji government inflicted on the former samurai. The abolition of the domains in 1871 disbanded the domain troops and stripped the samurai of the pensions and organisation that had sustained them; the sword ban of 28 March 1876 restricted the carrying of arms, and the stipend settlement of August cut pensions again, so that within months the middle and lower ranks of the samurai around Akizuki, Toyotsu and Saga passed from a secure living to short means. Behind this lay the political weather after the Freedom and People's Rights movement and the debate over the invasion of Korea: Saigo Takamori had resigned and gone home, and the Satsuma private academy ran both a rifle school and an artillery school, so that plans for defiance were held together through schools, domain academies and ties of locality, while the local authorities, replacing the old domain's role in policing, ensured that a clash would come sooner or later. The immediate trigger was the Shinpuuren rising in Kumamoto on the night of 24 October, in which the Shinpuuren party attacked the residences of the garrison commander and the prefectural governor, occupied the artillery barracks, and was crushed within a day. The news reached Chikugo within three days, and the Akizuki party, which had already arranged to rise together with the Toyotsu samurai, duly assembled at night on 27 October.
impact: 秋月之亂本身規模有限，四天內便告瓦解，但它把幾件事擺到政府面前。第一，舊藩士跨藩的聯繫網仍然存在：豐津藩士幾乎同時被牽動，佐賀也有人前往聯絡，事件呈現由一縣向三縣擴張的聯絡狀態。第二，鎮台制下的常備軍與新式警察在數日內確實能壓制數百人的武裝，但熊本砲兵營在開火的第一夜便被叛軍奪去，火砲與彈藥的保管集中、分置不足，是明顯的薄弱環。第三，縣警出現第一位殉職者，說明地方治安機構開始直接承擔武裝衝突的風險。鎮壓本身也推動了制度改革：明治九年十一月八日司法卿大木喬任公佈的臨時暴徒處分例，成為此後處理士族反亂的常設法令；乃木希典因情報與果斷得到山縣有朋的信任，半年後的西南戰爭中被派為先遣；西南戰爭之後，鎮台改組為師團並縮減兵員，常備軍逐步取代士族武裝。
impactEn: The Akizuki rising was small and was over in four days, but it laid several matters in front of the government. First, the old cross-domain network of samurai ties still existed: the Toyotsu men were implicated almost at the same moment, and men had already travelled to Saga, so that the affair showed a lattice of contacts spreading from one prefecture to three. Second, the permanent army under the garrison system and the new police could indeed crush several hundred armed men within days, but the Kumamoto artillery barracks was taken by the rebels on the very first night of the firing: guns and ammunition were stored too centrally and not dispersed enough, a clear weak point. Third, the prefectural police produced its first man killed on duty, showing that the local security organs had begun to bear the risk of armed clash directly. The suppression itself also drove institutional reform: the provisional brigand disposal ordinance promulgated on 8 November 1876 by Minister of Justice Ōki Takakatsu became the standing statute for dealing with samurai risings thereafter; Nogi Maresuke, trusted by Yamagata Aritomo for his intelligence and decisiveness, was sent as the advance guard in the Seinan War half a year later; and after that war the garrisons were reorganised into divisions and their strength cut, so that the permanent army gradually replaced the armed samurai.
result: 結果是政府方的完勝與叛方的慘敗。十月二十七日舉兵，三十日夜退入江川村栗河內，三十一日隊伍解散，磯淳、宮崎車之助、土岐清等七名士族在谷中自刃；抗戰派的今村百八郎帶二十六人折回秋月，攻擊設在秋月小學的討伐本部，殺死兩名縣廳高官，燒毀拘押反亂士族的酒屋倉庫，之後分散逃亡，十一月二十四日被捕；益田靜方早在十月二十六日赴佐賀的途中即被拘捕。十二月初三日福岡臨時裁判所宣判，今村與益田即日斬首，約一百五十名同黨受到懲役、除族等處分，豐津藩的杉生十郎等人因決定不舉兵而免於戰場。事件的代價同樣清楚：受處分者多數是知行數百石、俸祿剛被秩祿處分削減的舊藩中級武士，士族的俸祿與名譽體系加速崩解；而同年年底的山口萩之亂與翌年一八七七年的西南戰爭接連爆發，說明反亂的真正能量並未因豐津一役的勝利而消失，只是被推遲，並在更大的戰場上爆發。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete government victory and a crushing rebel defeat. The rising began on 27 October; the band fell back into Kakkawa-uchi in Egawa village on the night of the 30th and dissolved on the 31st, and seven samurai including Iso Jun, Miyazaki Kuranosuke and Toki Kiyoshi cut their own throats in the valley. The irreconcilable Imanaga Hyakuhachiro turned back with twenty-six men into Akizuki, assaulted the suppression headquarters in the primary school, killed two senior prefectural officials, burned the liquor warehouse where rebellious samurai were being held, and then scattered; he was arrested on 24 November. Masuda Shizukata had already been taken on the road to Saga on 26 October. On 3 December the Fukuoka Temporary Court pronounced sentence: Imanaga and Masuda were beheaded on the spot, about one hundred and fifty of their comrades were sentenced to penal servitude, removal from clan and the like, and Sugo Juro and the other Toyotsu men escaped the battlefield because they had decided not to rise. The cost is equally clear: those punished were mostly middle-ranking domain samurai with several hundred koku of income whose pensions had just been cut by the stipend settlement, and the samurai system of pensions and honour broke down faster than before. And in late October of the same year the Hagi rising broke out in Yamaguchi, followed in 1877 by the Seinan War, showing that the real energy of the samurai resistance had not been destroyed by the victory at Toyotsu; it had only been deferred, to burst on a larger field.
